child.simple_meaning_en: Young explorer, Grandpa Valluvar teaches us: Inglorious births are produced by the confusion (of mind) which considers those things to be real which are not real.
child.kutty_story_ta: இனியா பள்ளி முடிந்து வீட்டுக்கு வந்ததும் தன் தாத்தாவுடன் பூங்காவில் அமர்ந்திருந்தான்/அமர்ந்திருந்தாள். அன்று 'மெய்யுணர்தல்' என்ற அதிகாரத்தில் உள்ள திருக்குறள் 351 பற்றி தாத்தா ஒரு சுவையான கதை கூறினார். The very next morning, Iniya put that virtue into action at school by helping a classmate with patience and warmth. The teacher smiled and praised how one small good habit brightened the entire classroom. From that day on, Iniya remembered that living truthfully and kindly brings lasting joy.

youth.analysis_en: From Truth-Conciousness (Ascetic Virtue), Kural 351 speaks directly to teens navigating studies, friendships, leadership, and digital choices: Inglorious births are produced by the confusion (of mind) which considers those things to be real which are not real. Instead of reacting impulsively or following crowd noise, applying this principle builds quiet resilience, sharper focus, and genuine credibility among peers.

child.simple_meaning_en: Little friend, here is the simple wisdom of this Kural: Let it not be thought that there is another birth for him whose mind having thoroughly considered (all it has been taught) has known the True Being.
